hook
A rocket weighs as much as a herd of elephants, yet it flies all the way to space. How?
balloon
Blow up a balloon and let it go. Air rushes out one way, and the balloon zooms the other way.
balloon
That's Newton's third law. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. A rocket works exactly the same way.
inside
Inside, it carries two giant tanks: fuel, and liquid oxygen. Space has no air, so a rocket must bring its own oxygen to burn.
engine
They mix and explode in the combustion chamber. The bell-shaped nozzle blasts the hot gas downward at over ten thousand kilometres per hour.
forces
Now two forces fight. Gravity pulls the rocket down. Thrust pushes it up.
liftoff
When thrust beats gravity, we have liftoff!
lighter
As fuel burns, the rocket gets lighter, so it speeds up faster and faster.
stages
Empty tanks are just dead weight, so the rocket drops them. These are called stages.
orbit
Here's the surprise. Reaching space isn't just about going up. To stay there, you must fly sideways, at about twenty eight thousand kilometres per hour.
orbit
So fast that as you fall, the Earth curves away beneath you. You keep falling, but you never hit the ground. That's an orbit!
outro
Push gas down, go up. Thanks, Newton! Follow for more science made simple.
